correctness.rationale: Explicit Wiman sextic reduction and nodal quotient verified over F5; tangent-cone discriminant nonzero and Res(A,B)=2(t²-2). The B,C,D pairwise and derivative resultants certify nine disjoint simple branch points over any algebraically closed field for t nonzero and t² not 2. Kummer Riemann–Hurwitz yields connected genus6 normalization and four ordinary nodes; prime-to-5 V4 splitting gives Jac(C) isogenous to Jac(D)^3. Exact coefficient derivation from h^2 yields the hyperelliptic Cartier determinant t^8, hence full ordinary rank. The standalone SymPy certificate was executed successfully; F5 counts are supporting checks only.

originality.rationale: The verified geometric literature contains the four-nodal Wiman–Edge family, genus-six geometry, and rationality of its single special Wiman fiber modulo five, but no corresponding uniform ordinary-locus classification or nonzero polynomial Cartier determinant for all its smooth characteristic-five members was identified. A characteristic-five family theorem is not implied by characteristic-zero automorphism structure or one degenerate fiber. The exhaustive parameter-uniform proof is additional. Full historical priority is not guaranteed: hidden classical theta/genus-two calculations might imply it.

value.rationale: Computing the ordinary versus nonordinary stratification of the entire smooth genus-six Wiman–Edge family is a natural geometric-arithmetic gap. A uniform Frobenius criterion is more than finite examples: the determinant t^8 shows the ordinary condition everywhere on the smooth locus, in contrast to the rational exceptional Wiman fiber at t=0. The Klein-four and genus-two quotient factorization explains the phenomenon structurally and makes it relevant to reductions of Jacobians and moduli of ordinary abelian varieties.
